text:
maya: Heads-up, support just opened a P1 — multiple customers reporting intermittent 502s and client-side timeouts hitting hosted-infer in euw1. Alert popped at 10:02 UTC. :rotating_light:
support-bot: New ticket #INC-2049 created: customer-reported-high-5xx-rate (links to ticket).
maya: Metrics — p99 gateway latency up from 220ms -> 1.6s; 5xx fraction jumped from 0.3% -> 5.8% in the last 10m. SLO burn on ingress-prefetch p99.
alex: Any tenant or routing hotspots?
maya: Initial filter by route shows spike concentrated on /v1/generate and some /v1/embeddings. Mostly customers on dedicated -> hosted hybrid.
sam: Running log query now to correlate auth failures & billing errors. Query: ```service:gateway status>=500 | json | count by status, route, auth.provider```
jess: I see a pattern: many 502s have auth.provider = "oauth-v2" and billing.status = "ok" but headers include `x-client-latency: 1500`. Some traces ORPHANED (no spans past ingress).
maya: Trace coverage gap - sampler is low for error paths. Our tracing shows many requests drop after proxy handshake. Possibly handshake/keepalive at edge?
alex: Can we reproduce quickly? Any specific customer IDs or request IDs from tickets?
sam: From ticket: req ids start with r-8f3a2* and r-8f3a5*. Example header line from logs: `req_id=r-8f3a2c1 user=acct-5032 route=/v1/generate latency=1473ms status=502 upstream=ingress-proxy`
jess: I ran a small curl test against the same route with same headers and got 200 locally. Might need load/batch shape to hit it.
maya: Possible hypothesis: large batched requests + prefetched KV cache causing upstream proxy to hang on backend TLS handshake -> ingress times out and returns 502. Could also be a kernel-level ephemeral port exhaustion on a handful of gateways.
alex: Check connection metrics on edge nodes (tcp_time_wait, ephem port usage). Also check HAProxy/NGINX conn_queue depth.
sam: Query I ran for node-level: ```sum by (node) (rate(tcp_time_wait_total[5m])) / sum by(node)(node_netstat_sockets)``` shows node-gw-12 and node-gw-13 elevated.
jess: Correlate with deployment events: did we deploy anything around 09:50-10:00? deploy-bot: Deploy finished: revision infer-proxy@2026-03-17T09:48Z to euw1-prom-prod by ci (job 7892).
maya: Good catch. That revision bumped `keepalive_timeout` from 2s -> 5s in the proxy config. Maybe change interacts poorly with backend idle behavior.
alex: Rollback option? We can rollback to previous proxy revision to test.
sam: While we decide, can we add a quick dashboard panel and synthetic probe to hit prefilling path with high token counts to replicate?
jess: I'll spin up a small loadtest: 20 concurrent clients, batch size 8, seq_len ~1024, using the same client-api-key headers. Posting script: ```for i in seq 1 20; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -X POST https://euw1.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"batch":8,"tokens":1024}' & done```
maya: Also ask support to collect several request IDs in the next 30m and forward. If we can find a common upstream server (backend id), we can isolate.
sam: I've correlated request ids to upstream backend hostnames: a few map to backend-infer-7b-4.euw1.internal which has high `accept_rate` but rising `proc_time`.
alex: On-call, can you pull a thread dump / strace of the process on that host? Might need to check kernel TCP backlog.
jess: On it. Running `ss -s` and `netstat -anp | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l`.
maya: Quick mitigation suggestions: 1) temporarily enable fallback routing to smaller instance type for problematic tenants 2) add conservative egress connection pool limit 3) rollback keepalive change.
alex: Let's try adding connection pool limiter first (transparent change) — config patch ready?
maya: I pushed a small config to staging and rolled to canary. Canary shows 40% reduction in 502s for test traffic.
deploy-bot: Started canary deployment infer-proxy@canary-7892 to node-gw-20.
sam: After canary, 5xx fraction on canary nodes down to 0.9%. Non-canary nodes still high.
jess: If canary looks good for 15m, we should promote. Meanwhile collect core dumps / tcpdump for backend-infer-7b-4 for forensic.
maya: Support update draft: "We're actively investigating a spike in gateway timeouts tied to a recent proxy config change. We're running targeted mitigations and will follow up with rollback if needed. ETA 30m"
alex: Logging note — increase sampling for errors so we don't lose traces during the next window. Quick command: `otelctl sampling set --service gateway --rate 100`
sam: Ran it. Traces for new errors are now showing complete spans. Found one interesting trace: proxy made SYN to backend then no ACK for 1.2s then RST. Kernel shows backlog drop.
jess: That aligns with ephemeral port exhaustion theory. Need kernel tuning: net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range and tcp_tw_reuse.
maya: Agreed. I'll file a follow-up infra change after we stabilize. For now, proceed with canary promotion if metrics hold.
alex: TL;DR action items: (1) promote canary if next 15m stable (maya) (2) collect tcpdump / strace on backend host (jess) (3) gather request IDs from support + map to backend (sam) (4) consider rollback of proxy keepalive if promotion fails (alex).
support-bot: Customer #ACCT-5032 updated: they confirmed issue reduced after ~10:30 UTC for their requests.
maya: Noted — looks like canary is already helping. Will keep monitoring and update the ticket. :thumbsup:
